ana: Heads up — noticed a regression on qwen2.5 canary: tail latency up ~18% on multilingual decode workloads (esp. zh/ja).

sam: Ugh. Which workload? beam/greedy? batch size?

ana: Greedy streaming, steady QPS 120, batch target 8, dynamic batching on. Problem starts after kv-cache warmup ~2k tokens.

li: Can you paste the profiler snapshot from the run?

ana: Pasted below (shortened):
```
rt-prof session=canary-qwen2p5
top hotspots:
 - attention_kernel_fft: 42% (increases after seq>1024)
 - kv_cache_copy: 18% (spikes at token 2048 boundary)
 - tokenizer.segmenter: 6% (multilang splits)
```

priyanka: attention_kernel_fft? We usually prefer fused_matmul for these configs. Why FFT got chosen?

kai: Kernel selector picks based on seq_len and head_dim heuristics. For qwen2.5 some of the head/kvdim math ends up favoring FFT when seq_len > 512 because estimated memory throughput is better. Could be an estimator bug.

sam: Related: I saw kv_cache_copy copying per-head instead of per-kv-block recently after that PR that changed kv layout (#4123). Could be an extra memcopy cost that shows up only when head/kvdim mismatch occurs.

ana: Here's a minimal repro command we used: `./run_infer --model qwen2p5 --seq 2048 --batch 8 --tokenizer zh --dynamic-batching on --profile`. Repro is consistent in canary.

li: I ran the same locally. Observed that for multi-ling inputs tokenizer emits more splits -> effective seq_len becomes ~1.2x. That pushes selector into the FFT branch at runtime. But FFT kernel in our build has a regression for head_count % 8 != 0 (kernel expects padded heads).

perf-bot: Automated alert: canary qwen2p5 latency increased 17.9% vs baseline. Trace: https://perf.redwood/canary/1865012345

priyanka: So two hypotheses: 1) tokenizer multilang splits increase seq and push a different kernel; 2) kv layout change adds memcopies that amplify the change. Both plausible.

kai: I dumped the kernel selector decision table for that run: `selector.log` snippet:
```
seq=1500 head_dim=96 head_count=48 model=qwen2p5 -> choose=fft_kernel
seq=900  head_dim=96 head_count=48 model=qwen2p5 -> choose=fused_matmul
```
Notice threshold around ~1024 seq.

sam: Quick mitigation: force fused_matmul for qwen2p5 until we fix FFT. We can flip model config in runtime: `model_overrides.qwen2p5.kernel_preference = fused_matmul`

ana: Agree — can we roll that on canary now?

kai: I'll push an override to canary and prod-beta. Doing a canary patch: `PATCH /config/models/qwen2p5` -> set kernel_preference. Rolling in 30s.

perf-bot: Deploy started for config change (canary). CI checks: ok.

priyanka: While that's rolling, let's capture a microprofile when FFT is chosen and after override. Need a diff of `attention_kernel_fft` assembly path to find why head%8 case is slow.

li: I looked at the FFT kernel: it assumes kv-width padded to 128 for vector lanes and does scalar fallback for remainder. That adds branch + mem ops when head_count*head_dim%128 != 0. For qwen2p5 kvdim=96*48=4608 -> 4608%128=0 (!) so puzzling. But the new kv layout PR changed packing: now we pack as (heads, kv_chunk) and sometimes insert 16-byte alignment per head which leads to extra gaps.

sam: So packing padding per-head increases effective memory stride -> worse cache locality -> FFT memory-bound -> slower.

ana: TL;DR: tokenizer -> longer seq -> selector picks FFT -> FFT suffers from packing-induced strided access -> memcopy and scalar tails -> latency regression.

kai: Action items:
 - (P0) force fused_matmul override for qwen2p5 canary/prod-beta (in flight) — kai
 - (P1) revert/adjust KV layout packing PR or add padding-aware estimator to kernel selector — sam/priyanka
 - (P1) add tokenizer language-aware estimated sequence multiplier so selector uses effective_seq not raw token count — li
 - (P2) add microbench harness for FFT path with varied per-head padding to reproduce locally — ana

priyanka: Also add a small eval with zh/ja corpus to perf tests to catch this earlier.

kai: Canary override applied. Perf-bot will run one test cycle.

perf-bot: Canary config override complete. New run queued.

ana: Rerun result in 10m: latency back to baseline within 2%. Good temporary fix.

li: For the medium term: I'll add a check in selector: compute effective_seq = seq * tokenizer_split_multiplier(lang, avg_token_bytes). Use corpus heuristics. If effective_seq > threshold use fused_matmul preference.

sam: I'll open PR to fix KV packing alignment and add selector awareness: #4521.

priyanka: Nice triage. Keep notes in the incident board. We should also record this as a kernel-selection regression test.

ana: Adding final note: watch for other multi-ling models (mixtral) — may be same issue.

kai: ack. I'll propagate override to mixtral canary after verification.

ana: Thanks all :thumbsup:
